claim: FDA approved donor-islet therapy for a narrow adult T1D population with recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management
population_or_model: Adults with T1D and recurrent severe hypoglycemia
design: Regulatory approval and supporting clinical studies
endpoint: FDA indication; glycemic control and severe hypoglycemia
follow_up: Per label and primary reports
cointerventions: Allogeneic islet infusion; immunosuppression required
limitations: Narrow selected indication; donor supply, invasive procedure, immunosuppression risks; not general cure
notes: Use label and primary reports for exact efficacy denominator and adverse-event rates

claim: In the phase 1-2 zimislecel study, 10 of 12 full-dose recipients were insulin-independent at day 365
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
design: Phase 1-2 study
follow_up: At least 12 months; insulin independence assessed at day 365
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small and short-term; selected cohort; interim analyses were not prespecified; insulin independence does not establish cure or freedom from immunosuppression
notes: The 14-person analysis included 2 part A participants and 12 full-dose participants in parts B/C; all analyses were interim and not prespecified. The published part C primary endpoint is recorded separately in EV-008.

claim: Serious neutropenia occurred in 3 of 14 participants in the zimislecel study
population_or_model: 14 participants in the phase 1-2 study who completed at least 12 months follow-up
design: Phase 1-2 safety analysis
follow_up: Study follow-up; 14 participants completed at least 12 months
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small cohort; the observed event count does not establish causation
notes: 3/14 participants had serious neutropenia; reported as the most common serious adverse event

claim: Two of 14 participants died during zimislecel study follow-up: one caused by cryptococcal meningitis and one due to progression of preexisting neurocognitive impairment
population_or_model: 14 participants in the phase 1-2 study who completed at least 12 months follow-up
design: Phase 1-2 safety follow-up
follow_up: Study follow-up; 14 participants completed at least 12 months
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Two deaths were observed in a small cohort; event occurrence and reported cause do not establish treatment causality
notes: The paper reported 2/14 deaths during follow-up: one caused by cryptococcal meningitis and one due to severe dementia with agitation associated with progression of preexisting neurocognitive impairment

claim: At 14 months, a single recipient of gene-edited donor islets had continued graft function without immunosuppression; insulin independence was not demonstrated
population_or_model: One person with longstanding T1D
design: First-in-human single-participant report and follow-up
follow_up: 14 months
cointerventions: Gene-edited allogeneic islets; no immunosuppressive drugs
limitations: One participant; exploratory endpoint; continued graft function does not establish insulin independence, efficacy, or population safety
notes: The 2026 NEJM report follows the same single recipient reported in 2025

claim: Vertex reported that VX-264 did not meet its efficacy endpoint in phase 1-2 and would not advance further in clinical development
population_or_model: People with T1D in the VX-264 phase 1-2 study
design: Sponsor-reported program update
follow_up: Company update dated 2025-03-28
cointerventions: Encapsulated allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; device intended to avoid immunosuppression
limitations: Sponsor announcement; analyzed denominator and endpoint-level outcome counts were not reported in the cited update; it does not establish the biological reason for insufficient efficacy
notes: Company said additional analyses were planned; analyzed denominator and detailed results were not provided; mechanism of failure remains unresolved from these sources

claim: FDA accelerated approval allows teplizumab to delay decline in endogenous insulin production in certain 8-17 year-olds with recently diagnosed stage 3 T1D
population_or_model: Pediatric patients age 8-17 with recent stage 3 T1D
design: Adequate and well-controlled trial; accelerated approval
endpoint: C-peptide surrogate endpoint; postapproval study required
follow_up: Per trial and regulatory documents
cointerventions: Anti-CD3 antibody; prescribed monitored course
limitations: Delay/preservation is not cure; surrogate endpoint; boxed warning for viral reactivation
notes: Separate from stage 2 onset-delay indication

claim: All 12 participants in full-dose zimislecel parts B/C were free of severe hypoglycemic events during days 90-365 and had HbA1c below 7%
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
design: Interim phase 1-2 analysis of full-dose parts B/C
endpoint: Part C primary endpoint: freedom from severe hypoglycemic events and glycemic threshold
follow_up: Severe hypoglycemic events: days 90-365; abstract does not explicitly establish the assessment time for the reported HbA1c below 7% finding
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small selected cohort; analyses were interim and not prespecified; the endpoint definition specified HbA1c below 7% or a decrease of at least 1 percentage point from baseline at one or more assessments between days 180 and 365, but the abstract does not explicitly connect the reported 12/12 HbA1c result to that window
notes: The abstract reports 12/12 participants were free of severe hypoglycemic events and had HbA1c below 7%; the endpoint-definition window is not asserted as the observed HbA1c result's timing. Do not conflate with the 14-person safety population.

claim: All 12 full-dose zimislecel participants spent more than 70% of time in the glucose target range of 70-180 mg/dL
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
design: Interim phase 1-2 analysis of full-dose parts B/C
follow_up: During follow-up through day 365; the abstract does not separately specify the time-in-range aggregation interval
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small selected cohort; interim analyses were not prespecified; exact aggregation interval for this time-in-range measure is not stated in the abstract
notes: The abstract reports more than 70% time in range for the 12 full-dose participants; the reporting interval is not separately specified

claim: All 14 zimislecel-study participants had detectable C-peptide after infusion, having had undetectable C-peptide at baseline
population_or_model: 14 participants in the phase 1-2 study who completed at least 12 months follow-up
design: Interim phase 1-2 study analysis
endpoint: Serum C-peptide detection during a 4-hour mixed-meal tolerance test to assess engraftment and islet function
follow_up: Baseline undetectable; post-infusion detection (exact post-infusion assessment time not specified in abstract)
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small cohort; C-peptide detection is evidence of graft function, not insulin independence or cure; exact assessment time is not stated in the abstract
notes: All 14 participants had undetectable baseline C-peptide and detectable C-peptide after zimislecel infusion; the abstract does not specify a single post-infusion time point

claim: One participant achieved sustained insulin independence beginning 75 days after autologous CiPSC-islet transplantation and reported at one year
population_or_model: One participant with type 1 diabetes
design: First-in-human phase I preliminary analysis
follow_up: Onset at day 75; reported in one-year preliminary analysis
cointerventions: Already receiving immunosuppressants for prior liver transplant, per Cell authors; this prevented assessment of immune responses to the autologous graft
limitations: Single participant; ongoing immunosuppression is an important co-intervention; no control group; does not establish durability or generalizability
notes: The Cell abstract reports insulin independence starting day 75 and one-year results.

claim: Time in target glucose range increased from 43.18% at baseline to 96.21% at month 4 after CiPSC-islet transplantation
population_or_model: One participant with type 1 diabetes
design: First-in-human phase I preliminary analysis
follow_up: Month 4 after transplantation
cointerventions: Already receiving immunosuppressants for prior liver transplant, per Cell authors; this prevented assessment of immune responses to the autologous graft
limitations: Single participant; uncontrolled observation; result is not comparable to studies with different CGM windows or populations
notes: The abstract gives baseline and month-4 values but not the CGM aggregation interval.

claim: Time in target glucose range was reported as greater than 98% after month 4 in the CiPSC-islet participant
population_or_model: One participant with type 1 diabetes
design: First-in-human phase I preliminary analysis
follow_up: Subsequent stable follow-up in the one-year report; individual assessment dates not stated
cointerventions: Already receiving immunosuppressants for prior liver transplant, per Cell authors; this prevented assessment of immune responses to the autologous graft
limitations: Single participant; abstract does not specify individual measurement dates or CGM aggregation interval
notes: The abstract says thereafter time in target range was greater than 98%.
outcome_timepoint: Thereafter; exact assessment dates not stated

claim: Glycated hemoglobin was reported at around 5% during stable follow-up after CiPSC-islet transplantation

design: First-in-human phase I preliminary analysis
follow_up: After month 4; abstract reports stable values thereafter and a one-year preliminary analysis but not exact measurement dates
cointerventions: Already receiving immunosuppressants for prior liver transplant, per Cell authors; this prevented assessment of immune responses to the autologous graft
limitations: Single participant; approximate value; timing of each HbA1c measurement is not stated in the abstract
notes: Do not apply the HbA1c observation to a fixed assessment window not explicitly stated in the abstract.
outcome_timepoint: Thereafter; exact assessment dates not stated

claim: The one-year CiPSC-islet report found no indication of transplant-related abnormalities in the single participant

cointerventions: Already receiving immunosuppressants for prior liver transplant, per Cell authors; this prevented assessment of immune responses to the autologous graft
limitations: The abstract does not provide an adverse-event count, detailed event table, or criteria for transplant-related abnormalities; absence of an indicated abnormality is not proof of safety
notes: The source wording is “no indication of transplant-related abnormalities” at one year.

claim: In the pooled Lantidra studies, 25 of 30 treated participants achieved insulin independence at some point
population_or_model: Adults with type 1 diabetes and recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management
design: Two open-label single-arm studies pooled in the prescribing information
endpoint: Participants who achieved any period of insulin independence
follow_up: Variable follow-up after first infusion; 0.3-14.5 years
cointerventions: Allogeneic deceased-donor islets; systemic immunosuppression
limitations: Small uncontrolled pooled population; follow-up and number of infusions varied; insulin independence does not establish freedom from immunosuppression or cure
notes: The label reports five participants had no days of insulin independence; duration categories are recorded in EV-018 and EV-019.

claim: In the pooled Lantidra studies, 21 of 30 treated participants were insulin-independent for at least one year
population_or_model: Adults with type 1 diabetes and recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management
design: Two open-label single-arm studies pooled in the prescribing information
endpoint: Participants with at least one year of insulin independence
follow_up: Variable follow-up after first infusion; 0.3-14.5 years
cointerventions: Allogeneic deceased-donor islets; systemic immunosuppression
limitations: Small uncontrolled pooled population; follow-up and number of infusions varied; insulin independence does not establish freedom from immunosuppression or cure
notes: The label's duration categories include 12 participants insulin-independent for 1-5 years and 9 for more than 5 years.

claim: The Lantidra prescribing information reports insulin independence for more than five years in 9 of 30 treated participants
population_or_model: Adults with type 1 diabetes and recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management
design: Two open-label single-arm studies pooled in the prescribing information
endpoint: Participants with more than five years of insulin independence
follow_up: Variable follow-up after first infusion; 0.3-14.5 years
cointerventions: Allogeneic deceased-donor islets; systemic immunosuppression
limitations: Small uncontrolled pooled population; follow-up and number of infusions varied; insulin independence does not establish freedom from immunosuppression or cure
notes: The prescribing information reports 9/30; the FDA approval announcement reports 10 participants exceeding five years. This tracker retains the prescribing-information figure and does not combine the discrepant reports.

claim: At least one serious adverse reaction was reported in 27 of 30 Lantidra recipients
population_or_model: Adults with type 1 diabetes treated in the two Lantidra studies
design: Two open-label single-arm studies pooled in the prescribing information; safety follow-up
endpoint: Participants with at least one serious adverse reaction
follow_up: 0.3-14.5 years after first infusion; mean 3 years (SD 3.7)
cointerventions: Allogeneic deceased-donor islets; systemic immunosuppression
limitations: Label-reported adverse reactions over variable follow-up and infusion exposure; this count does not establish that every reaction was caused by the cell product
notes: The label states serious reactions were reported in 27 (90%) of subjects; serious reactions include procedural and immunosuppression-associated risks.

claim: Two of 30 Lantidra recipients died during follow-up
population_or_model: Adults with type 1 diabetes treated in the two Lantidra studies
design: Two open-label single-arm studies pooled in the prescribing information; safety follow-up
follow_up: 1.6 and 9.7 years after first infusion
cointerventions: Allogeneic deceased-donor islets; both participants were receiving immunosuppression at the time of the event
limitations: The label reports one death from multi-organ failure with sepsis and one from progressive confusion, global atrophy, and micro-ischemic disease; events during follow-up do not establish product causality
notes: The prescribing information reports 2/30 deaths (7%); both subjects were on immunosuppression at the time.

claim: Discontinuation of immunosuppression was followed by loss of islet-cell function in 8 of 30 Lantidra recipients
population_or_model: Adults with type 1 diabetes treated in the two Lantidra studies
design: Two open-label single-arm studies pooled in the prescribing information
endpoint: Loss of islet-cell function after immunosuppression discontinuation
follow_up: After discontinuation during variable follow-up
cointerventions: Allogeneic deceased-donor islets; systemic immunosuppression was used to maintain islet-cell viability
limitations: The label reports loss of islet-cell function and, when achieved, insulin independence after stopping immunosuppression; observational label data do not quantify a separate causal effect of the cell product
notes: The prescribing information describes this in 8 (27%) subjects; do not interpret insulin independence as evidence that graft function persists after immunosuppression cessation.
